authoredFrom: Input (built in tests/storage/producer-loss.test.ts from queue-count-overflow.json, seed et005b-queue-count-overflow): simulation.started at 10 ms (eventSeq 1); a job without cargo.loaded or market at 20 ms (2); 260 identical tolls of 5 at 30 ms (3-262); job.delivered at 250 ms (263) and the clear at 260 ms (264). No frame step, so there are no snapshots and both checkpoints show no job (docs/simulator-v1.md, OD-5 S7; J9 cannot open a late-attach trip). Transport: a durable client at 0 ms whose ACKs are withheld, a disconnect at 100 ms, a durable client at 200 ms that commits and acknowledges each item, and a disconnect at 300 ms. One service.

Storage stall: the test-only fault worker holds the commit of eventSeq 1 inside its transaction (R13). Nothing commits while it is held, so the consumer can acknowledge nothing; the first connection's scripted withhold is the producer-side view of that stall, and the test checks that no ACK is written before the release. Every item of the first connection queues behind the held commit: 255 events and 7 delta gaps, 262 items, below the application's backlog bound of 512 (ET-015c G11), so no BACKLOG_FULL closes the connection. The commit is released once the second connection's redelivered eventSeq 1 has reached the ingestion, and the rest of that connection is passed on only after storage reports coverage 262, so at most 264 items are ever pending.

Producer (protocol v1 §9, full store): with no ACK, events 1-255 are retained and the tolls 256-262 are lost as queueCount, each written while connected as its own delta gap, queueCount 1, both lost times at the toll's occurrence (1,000,030,000,000 ns). The producer's 256-entry bound therefore overflows long before the application's 512-item bound. The second connection's checkpoint reports A = 0 and nextEventSeq 263; it redelivers 1-255 and the merged record [256, 262] (queueCount 7, redelivered), then 263 and 264 are admitted live.

Trips are reasoned as in queue-count-overflow-trip.rows.expected.json from docs/trips.md: the job (2) is configured while running (T12), so trip@2 opens `unknown` with no cause interval; tolls 3-255 are attributed `trip` (T14); the gap [256] closes it {none, gap, partial} at the last label, the toll 255 (1,800,000,000,030, T15), with a trip-level event-loss interval of its new suffix (T10, trip-reducer case 8); the gaps [257]-[262] are session-level event-loss intervals. On the second connection the redelivered 1-255 are duplicates and the merged gap is `covered` (docs/storage.md, Coverage), so nothing is stored or applied twice; job.delivered (263) has no open trip and is `ambiguous` (T14); the clear (264) adds nothing.
Attributions use one hand-written abbreviation: an entry with `eventSeqRange` [first, last] stands for one attribution per eventSeq in that range, in order; the test expands it before comparing.

Counts: 264 first commits (255 events and 7 gaps of the first connection after the release, without an ACK; 263 and 264 live), 255 duplicates and 1 covered gap. Losses (G6): lostEvents 7, eventLoss 7, each counted once at its first commit.
